paper_title: Device and Runtime Heterogeneity Dominate Delivered Latency: Benchmarking Mobile Vision Transformers for Fine-Grained Classification on Commodity Smartphones
paper_abstract: Latency measured on a single reference handset is usually not a reliable basis for deployment decisions. Field devices differ in hardware and runtime backend, so architectures that appear efficient in published benchmarks may be recommended incorrectly for the devices that actually run them. This work aims to bridge this gap. Three mobile architectures–MobileNetV2-100, MobileViT-XXS, and EfficientFormerV2-S0–are benchmarked on 2,721 medicinal plant species (303,165 images) under four preprocessing variants and three seeds, against a ViT-Base/16 ceiling trained on identical partitions, and six deployed LiteRT artifacts are measured on three commodity Android handsets. The findings suggest that latency characterizes the device–model–runtime triple rather than the network alone: identical artifacts span 188 ms to 5341 ms, the fastest architecture on one handset is slowest on another, and the deployment recommendation reverses when a second device enters the benchmark. Half-precision conversion halves artifact size without reducing latency. The findings further suggest that EfficientFormerV2-S0 recovers 81.4% of the ceiling with 4.9% of its parameters, whereas MobileViT-XXS trails MobileNetV2-100 because its classifier head consumes 47.9% of its parameters. Engineered preprocessing reduces accuracy in all 45 paired comparisons. These results support multi-device benchmarking as a practical prerequisite for deploying offline intelligent classifiers in the field.

paper_title: Can Hidden Reasoning Stay Hidden? A Survey of Chain-of-Thought Extraction Attacks on Large Reasoning Models
paper_abstract: Providers of large reasoning models withhold the chain-of-thought (CoT) that their models generate, returning an answer, a short summary, and, in some APIs, an encrypted copy of the trace in order to prevent distillation and keep sensitive intermediate content private. Five studies published between March and September 2026 show how API clients can recover existing traces or obtain useful reasoning despite this restriction. This survey organizes that work at the level of threat models, mechanisms, and evaluation protocols. We formulate CoT extraction, compare the attackers that the studies assume, and group the attacks into three families according to how they obtain the trace: reconstruction from visible outputs, elicitation into a visible channel, and replay of the trace that the model has already produced. We then summarize how the attacks are evaluated, map the proposed defenses onto the families they address, and identify open problems. The surveyed evaluations establish that no single defense is effective across all three families, and comparing attacks requires a shared trace reference and separate measures of textual fidelity, task preservation, and downstream utility. We conclude by identifying several research gaps and open questions for future research.

paper_title: Quantum Image Encryption: A Comprehensive Review of Representations, Encryption Schemes, Security Evaluation and Open Challenges
paper_abstract: Quantum image encryption (QIE) loads a digital image into qubits and ciphers it with unitary circuits, usually keyed by chaotic maps, quantum walks or quantum random numbers. This review follows the field from an early geometric-transformation scheme (2013) to designs executed on 127-qubit IBM processors (2025). We organise the literature by image representation (FRQI, NEQR, amplitude encoding), confusion and diffusion mechanism, key source and validation level, and we compare recent schemes on entropy, NPCR, UACI, correlation and key space. Reported statistics sit close to their ideals almost everywhere; recent quantum-walk and chaos-based designs report NPCR of 99.6 to 99.97% and UACI of 33.5 to 33.9%, so these metrics no longer separate strong schemes from weak ones. Three gaps stand out. Most evidence comes from classical simulation. The secret usually sits in a classical key generator rather than in the quantum circuit. And loading an image into qubits, then reading it back, remains the main hardware bottleneck. Hybrid designs that distribute keys with BB84 and cipher the image classically offer the most deployable route today. We close with a research agenda: attack-based benchmarks, error-aware hardware validation, cheaper state preparation and explicit security definitions.

paper_title: [18F]FE-MPC6827: Improved Preparation and In Vitro Evaluation as PET Tracer for Imaging Microtubule Dynamics
paper_abstract: Microtubule (MT) dysfunction is a hallmark of neurodegenerative diseases, tauopathies, and genetic disorders. Positron emission tomography (PET) enables non-invasive assessment of MT dynamics in vivo, but current 11C-labeled radiotracers are limited by the short half-life of carbon-11. Here, we report the radiosynthesis and in vitro evaluation of [18F]FE-MPC6827, an 18F-labeled derivative of the brain-penetrant MT-destabilizing agent MPC-6827 (verubulin). Radiosynthesis from the corresponding tosylate precursor afforded [18F]FE-MPC6827 in 60±3% radiochemical yields (n=22), >99% radiochemical purities, and molar activities up to 475 GBq/µmol. Physicochemical profiling revealed a logD7.4 value of 3.37±0.05 and favorable CNS-MPO, BBB, and CNS-PET-MPO scores, indicating suitable properties for brain imaging. In HEK293T cells, MT destabilization significantly increased tracer accumulation, whereas MT stabilization significantly reduced uptake. Overexpression of MT-associated proteins (TAU, SPASTIN, MARK, α-tubulin) produced directionally consistent but statistically non-significant changes in tracer uptake concordant with effects on MT mass or stability. Across experiments, tracer uptake correlated inversely with MT stability. These findings suggest that [18F]FE-MPC6827 preferentially binds to depolymerized tubulin and responds to global shifts in MT dynamics, but may be less sensitive to subtle or localized cytoskeletal changes. Taken together, [18F]FE-MPC6827 is a promising first-in-class radiofluorinated PET tracer for imaging MT dynamics in the central nervous system.

paper_title: The Judge Under Trial: Stress-Testing RART and the Limits of Automated Evaluation at Scale
paper_abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) as automated evaluators commonly termed LLM-as-a-Judge introduces a critical question: who evaluates the evaluator? This paper puts the lifecycle framework of Kong et al. [1] on trial, stress-testing its core claims for building, aligning, and monitoring LLM judges in production-scale recommendation explanation systems. We synthesize the core contributions: (1) the identification of a subtle failure mode termed ”right answer, wrong reason,” wherein a judge reaches the correct verdict through unsound reasoning that is invisible to label-agreement dashboards; (2) Reasoning-Aligned Rubric Tuning (RART), a procedure that iteratively refines rubric text using a Meta-Judge to compare judge rationales against human rationales; (3) a fourphase lifecycle-Birth, Training, Deployment, and Monitoring-that anchors LLM judges to human judgment at every stage; and (4) a formal mathematical model stress-tested via Monte Carlo simulation. We provide an open-source implementation of this simulation and analyze its visual output. The simulation confirms RART’s ability to stabilize reasoning alignment but visually reveals methodological vulnerabilities, including a stopping-rule artifact, a severe drift-band calibration problem, and the structural reality of blind-spot leaks. Furthermore, the framework relies on critical unvalidated assumptions-most notably, that the judge and generator do not share blind spots. We conclude that while RART effectively mitigates rubric degradation, it is not a closed-form mathematical solution to Al alignment and ultimately requires continuous human-in-the-loop audits.

paper_title: Cyberattack Dataset Engineering and Benchmarking for Realistic Intrusion Detection: A Survey
paper_abstract: Intrusion detection research depends on datasets. However, dataset design is often treated as secondary to model selection. In this survey, we examine cyberattack dataset engineering and benchmarking for realistic intrusion detection system (IDS) evaluation. Specifically, we review dataset releases, benchmark critiques, and domain-specific detection studies that cover general-purpose network benchmarks, Android spyware, multi-step and APT-inspired attacks including SUNBURST, smart-grid injection, SNMP-MIB and DDoS monitoring, IoT botnets, phishing, streaming traffic, and GAN-based synthetic attack data. We argue that dataset realism must be judged through collection context, attack procedure, benign behaviour, labeling, feature extraction, temporal splitting, privacy, reproducibility, and benchmark saturation, rather than through dataset size or reported accuracy. To this end, we position the survey against prior IDS and dataset reviews, introduce a six-dimensional dataset-centred taxonomy (attack environment, data representation, collection method, label strategy, evaluation protocol, and threat model), compare seven dataset families, and consolidate an evaluation protocol that covers split policy, leakage checks, baselines, metrics, and dataset documentation. We conclude that next-generation IDS datasets should be released with dataset cards, scenario cards, leakage reports, baseline scripts, chronological and holdout splits, adversarial and zero-day partitions, and explicit limitations. This shift would make IDS results more comparable, make inflated performance claims easier to detect, and support realistic evaluation for IoT, 5G, smart grids, Android malware, phishing, and APT-inspired attacks.

paper_title: Knowledge, Information Sources, Attitudes, and Personal Use of Complementary and Integrative Therapies Among Undergraduate Nursing Students: A Pre–Post Educational Intervention Evaluation
paper_abstract: Background: Complementary and integrative therapies (CITs) are increasingly demanded, yet formal university training remains limited. This study evaluated overall knowledge, information sources, attitudes, and personal use of CITs among undergraduate nursing students before and after a dedicated course. Methods: A quasi-experimental study with two aggregated cross-sectional evaluations (pretest/posttest) was conducted in a second-year nursing cohort (N=135). An ad-hoc validated questionnaire was administered anonymously at baseline (n=106) and after completing an obligatory course on evidence-based complementary care (n=110). Results: Following the educational intervention, overall CIT knowledge expanded across the cohort. The university course became the predominant information source (87.3%), reducing reliance on social media (59.1%) and increasing consults of scientific literature (33.6%). Overall, 100 % of post-intervention respondents acknowledged the necessity of CIT knowledge for patient education. Support for mandatory curricular inclusion rose from 12.3% to 36.4%, while 56.4% favoured public healthcare integration conditional upon proven efficacy and safety. Conclusions: Course completion was associated with higher overall CIT knowledge, a shift toward evidence-based information sources, and favourable professional attitudes at the group level. Integrating evidence-based CIT education into nursing curricula is essential for fostering safe clinical practice.

paper_title: Recursive Self Improvement for Embodied Agents—A Survey of Mechanisms Evaluation and Open Challenges
paper_abstract: Embodied foundation models have expanded the range of instructions, observations, and actions that robots can process. Autonomy in execution, however, does not automatically provide autonomy in improvement. Robots must still diagnose failures, acquire useful experience, select interventions, and determine whether accepted changes improve future performance. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) connects these activities through persistent feedback and inheritance, with the stronger objective of improving the mechanisms that produce subsequent improvements. This survey distinguishes within-episode correction, persistent self-improvement, successive version inheritance, and meta-level improvement. It connects large-model learning, sequential agency, and RSI theory, and compares general agent harnesses with their embodied counterparts. It develops a four-axis framework covering improvement targets, update mechanisms, autonomy over improvement decisions, and evidence conditions. Using this framework, we examine reflection and knowledge revision, executable-program evolution, adaptive experience acquisition, parameter learning, world-model revision, and cross-layer intervention selection. We compare representative systems while retaining their assumptions about feedback, validation, transfer, and cost. We also review benchmarks and associated datasets for manipulation, long-horizon decision making, memory, and world modeling, separating pretraining data, improvement experience, candidate validation, and final evaluation. Existing results support several forms of component-level and system-level improvement, but capability gains, improvement autonomy, and demonstrated recursive gains require different evidence. We identify failure attribution, reliable feedback, physical reset, competence preservation, and independent evaluation of revised improvers as central research priorities.

paper_title: A New Holistic Oxygen, Carbon Dioxide, Climate & Seawater Evaluation (HOCCSE) Method of Halite Fluid Inclusions
paper_abstract: Halite, with primary fluid inclusions, is an invaluable archive of past oceanographic, climatic and atmospheric conditions – windows into the geologic past. This is particularly important for time intervals that lack, or have limited, biological evidence that can be used to constrain atmospheric oxygen levels. Everything from physical observations to petrography, geochemistry, microthermometry and mass spectrometry are critical in determining the best-preserved material. The proposed Holistic Oxygen Carbon dioxide Climate and Seawater Evaluation (HOCCSE) method fulfills this requirement, but it applies only to fluid inclusions in halite that contain trapped air bubbles varying in size from the nano- to macro-scale. The constraining factors for recognizing bubbles are their respective N2/Ar ratios and argon contents, thus by definition, it excludes atmospheric gas dissolved within the fluid of the inclusions. Liquid-vapor homogenization temperatures (Th°C) and measured CO2 contents serve a dual purpose in characterizing both ambient (local) and global climate conditions. Furthermore, the atmospheric gas parameters are useful in defining the temperature, dissolved oxygen and pH of the formation waters/brines. Using the HOCCSE method we re-examined the halite of the Tonian Browne Formation (Officer Basin, Australia). The initial presentation of our results (Blamey et al., 2016) led to considerable debate as to the environmental environment of the Earth during the Tonian and how it fits into the generally modeled conditions. The entrapped air suggest that the Tonian atmosphere consisted of the following gases (adjusted for humid conditions): 84.19 % N2, 9.99 % O2, 0.831 % Ar and 0.951 % CO2. Th°C of local seawater range from 34 to 41°C, which are slightly higher than those calculated using Climate Sensitivity equations and adjusted for a fainter sun, range from 27–30°C. However, when the warming contribution of methane to the climate is considered, the increased temperatures vary from 32 to 38°C. Seawater conditions during this period were quite suitable for marine life requiring at least 100 µmol/kg of dissolved oxygen and a pH of greater than 7.5. These atmospheric, seawater and climate parameters support the concept that Tonian conditions resembled a hothouse, but with environmental conditions suitable for a habitable and biologically evolving Earth.

paper_title: Localized Maxwell-Stress Excitation and Modal Eigenvalue Analysis for Vibroacoustic Characterization of Switched Reluctance Machines
paper_abstract: This paper presents an integrated, tooth-resolved electromagnetic-structural framework linking localized Maxwell surface tractions to three-dimensional stator dynamics and equivalent radiated power in a three-phase 6/4 switched reluctance machine. Transient radial and tangential force vectors are extracted from a two-dimensional finite-element model across six distinct stator tooth tips and mapped directly as remote nodal force resultants onto a three-dimensional solid structural continuum mesh. Baseline and modified geometric configurations are contrasted across matched multi-axial speed-frequency envelopes. The modified layout suppresses peak absolute tangential-force excursions, while radial peak loads are redistributed temporally rather than uniformly minimized. All six reported natural frequencies decrease non-uniformly; the fundamental mode drops by 34.01% from 3166.3 to 2089.5Hz, maintaining a safe separation margin above the 1000Hz excitation band threshold. Consequently, the modified configuration yields uniform attenuation across both the 0–250Hz forced deformation response curves and the non-overlapping decibel waterfall scales. These results demonstrate that vibroacoustic attenuation stems from the coupled phase interactions of the structural compliance matrix and multi-axial loading vectors rather than single-parameter force minimization, establishing a highly reliable numerical radiation indicator for design-stage benchmarking.

paper_title: Toward Sensory Homeostasis in Autism: Comparative Evaluation of a Recurrent Signal-to-Memory Hierarchy
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: The signal-to-memory (S2M) hierarchy links Ca²⁺-signal construction and decoding to transcriptional and chromatin changes that may modify subsequent neuronal responsiveness and support sensory homeostasis: adaptation to familiar input while preserving sensitivity to meaningful change. We assessed evidence for its involvement in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) pathogenesis and implications for therapeutic target validation. Methods: The prespecified S2M-44 core was compared with 11 monogenic ASD mouse models, an ASD protein-association network, and 106 schizophrenia-prioritized genes. Exact overlap, molecular association, and functional correspondence were distinguished; broader ASD-gene context and four extension candidates were evaluated separately. Results: Four mouse-model genes matched the core, all transcriptional or chromatin regulators. The protein network represented 27 core proteins, including both IP₃ receptors, ITPR1 and ITPR3, recovered as interactors. Separately reported KDM6B and SETD5 studies demonstrated rescue of downstream neuronal defects, with selected behavioral rescue in the SETD5 model. The schizophrenia set shared one core gene and implicated related signaling operations. Conclusions: These findings strengthen the case for pathogenic involvement of connected S2M operations and prioritize IP₃R-mediated Ca²⁺ release for molecular target validation. Demonstrating target-dependent restoration of signaling and adaptive responsiveness across genetically distinct models would establish a mechanistic foundation for drug discovery.

paper_title: Evaluating Machine Learning Model Behaviour for Temporally Structured Crime-Count Prediction
paper_abstract: Predicting crime counts is a difficult technology problem because the data are temporally dependent, uneven across locations and categories, vulnerable to leakage, and often dominated by persistence from prior periods. This study evaluates how distinct machine-learning (ML) regression families behave when applied to temporally structured crime-count data and asks whether increased model complexity produces measurable improvements over a simple seasonal benchmark. This study evaluates five ML regression families - Random Forest Model (RFM), Extreme Gradient Boosting Regressor (XGBR), K-Nearest Neighbor Regressor (KNNR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Multi-Layer Perceptron Regressor (MLPR) - compared across alternative categorical encoding scenarios (S), while Seasonal Naïve (SNa-ïve) prediction was retained as a transparent benchmark. The experimental protocol used rolling-origin tuning over 2019–2023, a separate 2024 validation period, and a one-pass 2025 held-out comparative evaluation of frozen candidate configurations. The 2025 observations were not used to define features, preprocessing rules, encoding scenarios, hyperparameter grids, or tuned hyperparameters. Because the trained configuration used for the later forecasting demonstration was chosen after inspection of the 2025 comparison, the 2025 scores are treated as comparative evidence across pre-specified candidates rather than as an independent post-selection validation of that forecasting choice. SNaïve achieved the lowest 2025 error (RMSE=44.162; MAE=21.224; R²=0.9669). Among the trained candidates, XGBR S4 had the lowest RMSE (56.449), followed closely by RFM S4 (57.088). Encoding choice affected trained-model behaviour, prediction intervals showed mild undercoverage, local error varied substantially, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis showed that the one-year same-quarter lag was the dominant explanatory feature. The 2026–2027 values are unvalidated model projections and are not findings about future crime outcomes. The paper therefore reports a bounded empirical comparison and reproducible temporal evaluation protocol for this administrative crime-count dataset; it does not claim universal crime prediction, hotspot detection, or a general operational decision rule.

paper_title: Comparative Clinical and Immunological Evaluation of Bulbar Conjunctival Pedicle Grafting and Allogeneic Canine Amniotic Membrane Grafting for the Management of Corneal Ulcers in Dogs
paper_abstract: Background: The cornea is a transparent, avascular, and highly specialized structure that serves as the eye’s primary refractive surface, making it essential for normal vision. Corneal ulcers, commonly resulting from trauma or infection, are a leading cause of ocular morbidity and blindness in dogs. Surgical intervention is often required for deep or non-healing ulcers. Conjunctival grafts help restore corneal integrity but may prolong recovery. Canine amniotic membrane (AM) possesses an-ti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and epithelialization-promoting properties that may enhance corneal wound healing. Methods: Twelve clinical canine cases with corneal ulcers were randomly allocated into two Groups (n = 6 each). Group A underwent bulbar conjunctival pedicle grafting, while Group B received canine amniotic membrane grafts prepared from placentas collected during elective cae-sarean sections. The amniotic membrane was applied in three layers and stabilized with a third-eyelid flap and partial tarsorrhaphy. Postoperative assessment included physiological pa-rameters, detailed ophthalmic examinations, tear production tests, fluorescein dye uptake, and rel-evant biochemical analyses. Results: Complete healing was achieved in five of six dogs in Group A and in all six dogs in Group B. Physiological and biochemical values did not differ significantly between Groups; however, Group B exhibited more rapid epithelialization, reduced postoperative complications, and overall better clinical recovery. Conclusion: Both surgical approaches were effec-tive in managing canine corneal ulcers, but the canine amniotic membrane graft provided superior healing, faster epithelial restoration, and improved clinical outcomes.

paper_title: Rapid Evaluation of Chaboche–Voce Material Model Parameters Through a Fully Reversed Strain-Controlled Test
paper_abstract: Modeling cyclic plasticity remains challenging due to the high computational cost of nonlinear constitutive models and the large number of parameters requiring evaluation, which are often temperature-dependent. This work presents a systematic procedure for identifying the parameters of the Chaboche–Voce model, one of the most widely adopted constitutive models for cyclic plasticity and commonly implemented in finite element software. Due to its nonlinear formulation, however, parameter evaluation is not straightforward. The parameters governing the kinematic hardening response are determined through a simple least-squares fit, yielding an analytical expression for a branch of the mid-life stabilized cycle. The Voce parameters are subsequently obtained by solving an analytical equation followed by a further least-squares fit. The resulting methodology provides a systematic approach for characterizing materials exhibiting both cyclic hardening and softening. The procedure was applied to two materials: 42CrMo4+QT tested at room temperature at different strain ranges for two different values of mean strain and 1Cr-1Mo-0.25V steel tested at different temperatures and strain ranges. The proposed approach provides satisfactory constitutive parameters while requiring virtually negligible computational cost, making it suitable for efficient material characterization and subsequent finite element implementation.

paper_title: AI in Education from CAI to AGI: A Narrative Review and Conceptual Framework
paper_abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping education, yet research remains fragmented across technological streams and often conflates technical capability with demonstrated educational effectiveness. This narrative review synthesizes representative literature published mainly between 2010 and 2026 to trace the evolution of AI-enabled education from computer-assisted instruction toward adaptive, immersive, generative, and potentially more general forms of intelligence. It compares three major technological streams: intelligent tutoring and adaptive learning systems, extended reality (XR), and large language model-based generative AI. The review finds that intelligent tutoring systems support learner modeling, adaptive feedback, and personalization, but their evidence base is methodologically heterogeneous. XR shows comparatively more consolidated evidence, particularly through systematic reviews and meta-analyses, with generally positive but context-dependent effects on engagement and learning outcomes. Generative AI expands dialogic explanation, scaffolding, content generation, and personalized support, although learner-outcome evidence remains limited relative to capability benchmarking. Building on these findings, the review proposes a Technology–Mechanism–Outcome–Challenge framework and argues that future progress toward artificial general intelligence (AGI) should be evaluated through learning mechanisms, measurable outcomes, human oversight, equity, and responsible governance.

paper_title: Cross-Dataset Evaluation of Interpretable Photoplethysmography Features for Blood Pressure Category Classification
paper_abstract: Photoplethysmography (PPG) provides waveform features for blood pressure (BP) category classification, but performance may vary across recording conditions. We evaluated a framework incorporating Step-Morphological Decomposition (SMD) on Aurora-BP, PPG-BP, PulseDB-Vital and the Synchronized Signals from Wearable Cardiovascular Monitoring Sensors dataset (SWCS). Signals were processed at 125 Hz. Conventional and neural classifiers were compared using subject-grouped evaluation, feature-family ablation, Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) and cross-cohort adaptation. On Aurora-BP, XGBoost achieved a mean three-class macro one-versus-rest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.778 ± 0.011 across five folds. Subject-aggregated binary prediction achieved AUC 0.841. Source-only AUCs were 0.662 ± 0.096 on PPG-BP, 0.556 ± 0.049 on PulseDB-Vital and 0.696 ± 0.083 on SWCS. A restricted PPG-only pipeline achieved AUC 0.704. Removing the SMD feature family changed AUC from 0.778 to 0.776. Period morphology had the largest summed SHAP attribution, whereas demographic predictors had the largest average attribution per feature. Adaptation effects varied across cohorts and available target data. These retrospective results characterize the performance and limitations of the evaluated feature framework. Prospective clinical screening performance was not evaluated.

paper_title: Chart Reasoning with Multimodal Large Language Models: A Survey
paper_abstract: Chart reasoning requires multimodal models to interpret visual encodings, derive structured semantics, execute formal reasoning procedures, and generate evidence-grounded outputs. This survey reviews chart reasoning methodologies for multimodal large language models (MLLMs), categorizing them by their primary intervention points: data and supervision design, inference-time reasoning strategies, and model-integrated optimization. We examine how existing approaches extract chart semantics, use intermediate representations, execute reasoning workflows, ground predictions in visual evidence, and verify outputs. We also summarize major chart reasoning benchmarks and cross-paradigm empirical results, and examine limitations in current evaluation protocols and metrics. Finally, we discuss recurring challenges in synthetic-to-real generalization, semantic reconstruction, visual grounding, reasoning faithfulness, and diagnostic evaluation, outlining directions toward more reliable and generalizable chart reasoning systems.

paper_title: Two Kinds of Inconsistency: A Constructive Note on the Empirical and Analytical Evaluation of the Energy Balance Model
paper_abstract: Arencibia-Albite presents two arguments against the Energy Balance Model: numerical tests showing that its predictions diverge from measurement, and an analytical proof showing that it is internally inconsistent when obligatory nitrogen loss is accounted for. These arguments are frequently treated as a single case. They are not. They describe two different kinds of failure, with different causes and different corrections. The analytical argument has been addressed elsewhere: when the chemical enthalpy carried out of the body by unoxidized nitrogen is included in the energy balance equation, the contradiction resolves – and the corrected model requires a mass-based term. The numerical argument is weakened by methodological asymmetries that can inflate the apparent empirical failure of the model. Absorption corrections applied asymmetrically across trial phases, and extrapolation from weekly chamber measurements to 14-day ward expenditure, can shift the calculated energy balance systematically. These asymmetries do not refute Arencibia-Albite's conclusion. They refine its evidential basis. When both arguments are corrected, what remains is a mass-based framework. This is not a critique of his work. It is its logical continuation.

paper_title: Tailored Induction for International Medical Graduates: Development and Evaluation of a Structured Onboarding Program at a UK Teaching Hospital
paper_abstract: International medical graduates (IMGs) constitute an increasing proportion of the UK medical workforce but often encounter professional, cultural, and practical challenges when transitioning into the NHS. At University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust (UHB), IMGs account for up to 75% of newly appointed locally employed doctors. In response to national guidance, UHB developed a tailored induction and onboarding program comprising a two-day, face-to-face course aligned with the four nationally defined induction domains. Delivered bimonthly by a multidisciplinary faculty, the program integrates interactive teaching, practical clinical skills training, simulated communication exercises, pre-arrival resources, peer support, digital learning materials, and a structured four-week integration period. Program evaluation included standardized quantitative and qualitative feedback from 213 participants across 14 induction cycles between May 2023 and July 2024. Mean satisfaction scores exceeded 4.5/5 for all sessions, with clinical skills and e-portfolio/appraisal sessions receiving the highest ratings (4.81/5). Participants reported improved confidence in clinical procedures, greater understanding of NHS systems, and increased confidence in career development. Feedback identified opportunities to expand IT systems training and optimize session scheduling. A structured, IMG-specific induction program can support successful transition into NHS practice, enhance preparedness for clinical work, and provide a scalable model for organizations recruiting international doctors.

paper_title: Decision Models as Product Rerankers for E-Business Search and Recommendation: An Independent Evaluation on the Amazon Shopping Queries Dataset
paper_abstract: Which products a shopper sees first, in search results or recommendations, shapes what they buy. Retailers increasingly use language models to judge product relevance. Decision models (Jev, Clef and Perplexity Decider) return a probability for each permitted judgement instead of generated text, which makes them natural rerankers for search and recommendation. We present, to our knowledge, the first independent, pre-specified evaluation of decision models on the Amazon Shopping Queries (ESCI) benchmark, with 1,000 US-English, 200 Spanish and 200 Japanese queries. Baselines were a dedicated reranker (Qwen3-Reranker-4B), general-purpose language models, a cross-encoder fine-tuned on 50,000 in-domain pairs, and BM25. Every decision model improved nDCG@10 over BM25, by 0.084 to 0.114 in English and by 0.100 to 0.149 in Spanish and Japanese (for Japanese, against a BM25 with character-bigram segmentation). Perplexity Decider ranked best (0.822) and significantly outperformed the dedicated reranker (0.787) by 0.032 to 0.035, whether run locally or through its hosted API. Asking for a four-way relevance label, an ordinal score or a yes/no exact-match judgement mattered little; the four-way label was best or tied in every comparison. All systems confused Exact with Substitute products; recall of Complement products, which underpin accessory recommendations, ranged from 15% to 68%. Clef’s labels were unaffected by the order of answer options, which it sorts internally, whereas a general-purpose language model changed up to 26% of its labels. The hosted Perplexity API reranked 1,000 queries for US$0.10–0.14 and, with the yes/no design, lay on the cost–quality frontier. We discuss implications for retailers, marketplaces, recommender systems and shopping agents.

paper_title: AEON: Unifying Video and 3D World Models
paper_abstract: Current world models for explicit world simulation typically follow two distinct pathways: (1) video generative models (e.g., Sora), which simulate realistic appearances but fail to preserve 3D consistency; and (2) 3D generative models (e.g., Marble), which generate geometrically consistent scenes but often yield static, less realistic observations. We present AEON, a unified framework that bridges video-based and 3D-based world models and combines the benefits of both. The key insight of AEON lies in a generative model that operates within the text- or image-conditioned video latent space while producing renderable 4D graphics primitives---specifically, 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS)---as the explicit world representation. We train a 4D reconstruction model to predict both 4DGS and camera poses from monocular videos, serving as our initialized 4D decoder. Furthermore, we design a domain adapter that translates generative video latents into reconstructive 4D latents through a distillation process on the video VAE. AEON naturally supports video-based world modeling by rendering 4DGS at predicted camera trajectories, and constructs a persistent 4D environment with scene dynamics for realistic world simulation. Consequently, AEON empowers a diverse range of world modeling applications and achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks. Project Page: https://weiqi-zhang.github.io/AEON
comments: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Project Page: https://weiqi-zhang.github.io/AEON

paper_title: SolarRenderer: Few-Step Generative Reference Rendering
paper_abstract: Game engines and coding agents can specify the layout, motion, and camera of a scene, yet turning such coarse structure into realistic video requires a renderer that follows the structure and completes the appearance it leaves open. Existing renderers are tied to the representation of one engine, need tens of denoising steps or a costly distillation of their own, and learn from conditions that are not aligned with their target videos. We present SolarRenderer, a structure-conditioned video renderer that adapts a frozen MiniMax-H3 33B backbone with two lightweight LoRAs. Structural videos enter the native reference pathway of the backbone at the positions of the frames they describe, without a type identifier and described only in plain text, so that a single control LoRA follows arbitrary structural representations. Starting from a pretrained four-step LoRA, structure-guided distribution matching renders in four steps, 12.3 times faster than 50-step sampling, while preserving the learned control. A block-causal variant extends the same design to streaming and renders 768p video in real time. To train the model, we build a frame-aligned corpus of 136K clips from game engines, simulators, and YouTube videos. Experiments on an in-distribution test set and a generalization benchmark of 16 structural representations show that SolarRenderer achieves state-of-the-art results across both, and generalizes to 11 unseen representations, including pose skeletons, drawings, and point clouds.
comments: Technical Report; 28 pages, 17 figures, 10 tables; Project page at https://enderfga.cn/SolarRenderer Code at https://github.com/Enderfga/SolarRenderer

paper_title: PsycheMME: A Psychology-Informed Benchmark for Social Understanding and Interaction in Videos
paper_abstract: Understanding human needs and selecting responses require distinct judgments that aggregate accuracy can obscure. We introduce PsycheMME, a video benchmark informed by psychology, with eight capabilities spanning grounding, states, needs, interaction decisions, memory, and risk. Drawing on Social Information Processing and the Perception-Action Cycle, this organization separates human understanding from response selection. We construct 1,000 questions from 630 episodes through independent answering with proposed references withheld and expert review. Our Reasoning-Verified protocol weights answer credit by the support and logical consistency of explicit rationales against annotated cues. Across 17 models, Timing has the lowest Verified scores and credit retention, with weaker support judgments for correct Timing answers. Models with similar Need scores still differ in answer completeness on open questions. Input controls and SFT/GRPO examine context dependence and adaptation. Evaluating answers alongside rationales locates where models fail across understanding, response selection, and justification.

paper_title: Planning under Noise with Neural Operators
paper_abstract: Planning under uncertain control execution noise requires reliable feedback policies across diverse environments. We introduce Planning Under Noise (PUN), a neural operator that learns noise-aware value fields for planning in unseen geometries. Building on an established screened-Poisson formulation of stochastic optimal control, we address two challenges: specifying boundary conditions that support navigation across varying geometries and efficiently computing fields with reliable gradients. Zero-Dirichlet obstacle boundaries terminate sampled paths at walls, weakening the goal signal along long routes and making it harder to estimate reliably. We instead impose reflecting Neumann conditions on obstacles and a Dirichlet condition at the goal, allowing sampled paths to continue exploring free space until they reach the target. To solve the resulting PDE without a configuration-space mesh, we extend a Monte Carlo (MC) solver, Walk on Stars (WoSt), to higher dimensions. However, local MC fluctuations can reverse estimated gradient directions and cause planning failures, making direct planning require costly sampling. PUN amortizes this computation by learning geometry-to-field mappings from noisy, partially converged Monte Carlo labels, avoiding expensive convergence for every training example. At inference, test-time scaling uses bounded local search guided by the predicted global field. We evaluate PUN on planning tasks across dimensions. Across four noise levels, PUN matches or outperforms all compared planners, achieving 95-100% success on the 4D replanning benchmark while maintaining the lowest runtime. At the highest tested noise level in 4D, PUN achieves 10.7-60.6% relative gains in success rate over other methods while running 3.29-32.15 times faster.

paper_title: MindView: Benchmarking Generative Multi-View Spatial Intelligence
paper_abstract: Spatial intelligence has recently been assessed through generative tasks such as spatially grounded image editing, yet language-guided generation of spatially consistent views from partial multi-view observations remains underexplored. We introduce MindView, a benchmark for generative multi-view spatial intelligence with 1,500 samples from 513 scenes across three indoor datasets. Its seven tasks form two families: geometry-dominant tasks specify changes in camera position and orientation, while semantics-dominant tasks require inferring target viewpoints by grounding referred objects and interpreting spatial relations and reference-frame cues. Evaluation of eleven generators reveals substantial room for improvement on MindView. A paired context analysis further shows that all eleven generators obtain lower overall scores under the expanded context setting. These findings motivate us to investigate whether task-specific supervision can improve target-view generation and whether models can use additional multi-view evidence effectively. We therefore fine-tune BAGEL on the MindView training dataset, improving its overall score by 24.3 points and yielding gains across all seven MindView tasks. Beyond these generation gains, the fine-tuned model also yields higher scores on three spatial-understanding benchmarks without training on their annotations, suggesting that learning to generate spatially grounded views may benefit spatial understanding. To improve evidence utilization under expanded context, we propose MindCue, a training-free spatial evidence selector guided by a target-view hypothesis. MindCue reverses the drop in overall score under expanded context and outperforms the standard-context baseline. Overall, MindView provides a concrete testbed for generative multi-view spatial intelligence.

paper_title: Semantic Observability for Autonomous Systems Diagnostics
paper_abstract: Modern distributed microservice deployments generate massive volumes of heterogeneous, multi-format observability logs across physically and logically partitioned infrastructure. Isolating root causes during cascading failures remains an arduous task for Site Reliability Engineers (SREs), bottlenecked by manual keyword filtering and disjointed temporal correlation across monitoring dashboards. We introduce Semantic Observability, an autonomous multi-agent framework that unifies disparate log streams into a dynamic, queryable Property Graph Database. By modeling physical infrastructure topologies, logical software dependencies, and chronological event sequences as attributed nodes and directed relations, it bridges the semantic gap inherent in flat, unstructured log repositories. Building on this unified substrate, we deploy a stateful multi-agent system orchestrated through Directed Cyclic Graphs (DCGs). The system autonomously navigates the topology, applying causal graph algorithms and temporal back-traversal to isolate the precise blast radius of anomalies. The pruned subgraph is then interpreted by a Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning engine to generate contextualized, code-level Root Cause Analyses (RCA) and actionable remediations. This paper establishes the foundational system architecture, formal relational ontology, and multi-agent control loops of Semantic Observability. We show conceptually how the framework eliminates ambient telemetry noise, reduces Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR), compresses LLM token consumption, and prevents structural hallucinations. We also specify an open-source validation framework on standard benchmarks (LogHub and Train-Ticket), laying the groundwork for a forthcoming companion paper on exhaustive quantitative evaluation and production benchmarking.
comments: 8 pages, 3 figures. Foundational architecture paper; companion evaluation paper forthcoming

paper_title: Benchmarking Arabic Dialects for Math Problems
paper_abstract: Mathematical reasoning remains underexplored for low-resource languages, including Dialectal Arabic. To bridge this gap, we introduce the DAR-MGSM (Dialectal Arabic Multilingual Grade School Math) Benchmark, the first manually curated benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning in Dialectal Arabic. DAR-MGSM consists of math word problems (MWPs) requiring multi-step reasoning and covers five major Arabic dialects alongside Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). The benchmark comprises two parallel versions: translated-only and translated & culturally localized. The latter version adapts entities and references to regional varieties. We evaluate eleven Arabic-centric and multilingual large language models on DAR-MGSM. The results show that the performance generally declines on the localized version, highlighting the challenges introduced by culturally grounded adaptations. However, the magnitude of this effect varies across models, with Arabic-centric models exhibiting different levels of sensitivity to localization. A mechanistic interpretability analysis shows that translated and localized variants of the same MWPs often induce distinct internal reasoning trajectories, even when aggregate accuracy remains similar. Overall, our results show that mathematical reasoning performance depends on both linguistic variety and cultural context.

paper_title: What Do RTL Repair Benchmarks Actually Measure?
paper_abstract: RTL repair benchmarks should measure whether a model can fix broken RTL given a specification. To this end, we construct and hash-bind RTLRepairDataset, 5,784 (broken, fixed) training pairs; RTLRepairBench, 459 held-out cases with 374 syntactic and 85 behavioral mutations; and an evaluation harness supporting simulation and formal equivalence. We then use this infrastructure to identify two measurement confounds. First, simulation and formal scoring give opposite signs for the apparent effect of providing a specification in one evaluated cohort; reset-aware rescoring attributes almost all of the simulation-formal disagreement to reset and first-cycle comparison semantics. Second, on 274 mined model failures, the specification-only minus specification-conditioned recovery point estimate ranges from -8.5 to +18.3 percentage points across six models. Thus, a conventional repair score need not isolate whether the model used the faulty RTL. We translate these findings into evaluation controls: report initialization, reset, first-cycle, and unknown-value semantics; disclose oracle coverage and undecided cases; and include a specification-only baseline. Together, the resources and audit provide both a benchmark for behavioral repair and a protocol for diagnosing what contributes to its measured score. We release the benchmark, the training set, construction code, sanitized aggregate evidence, and reproduction materials at https://github.com/Evaaaz/RTLRepairBench.

paper_title: Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting
paper_abstract: Reliable multi-view forecasting requires videos from different cameras to describe the same evolving 3D scene. To this end, we introduce Video-Point Model (VPM), a world model that conditions on multi-view video histories and a language instruction to jointly forecast future videos from arbitrary viewpoints and the 3D trajectories of persistent scene points. We extend a pretrained world model with camera-conditioned multi-view processing that integrates complementary observations across cameras, and add a trajectory head that predicts how physical points move through time. Each trajectory tracks a single point across all views, and supervising these trajectories alongside video generation therefore anchors appearance changes in every camera to a shared description of 3D motion. To support training and evaluation, we build VPM-Data, a simulation corpus pairing synchronized multi-view videos with persistent point trajectories, and VP-WorldBench, a forecasting benchmark spanning simulated and real environments. We further extend VPM to robot control by adding robot actions as a token modality in the generator. Action tokens share the point-supervised backbone and are denoised jointly with future videos, thereby grounding the policy in the same 3D-aware representation. On VP-WorldBench and existing 4D generation benchmarks, point supervision improves both video fidelity and 3D motion accuracy over a video-only counterpart, and in simulated and real-robot experiments, it also raises the manipulation success of the action-enabled model.

paper_title: Beyond the Sequentiality Bottleneck: A Hybrid Diffusion-Autoregressive Framework for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
paper_abstract: Autoregressive models (ARMs) face a "Sequentiality Bottleneck" in reasoning, while diffusion language models (DLMs) offer parallelism but lack semantic coherence. To addresses both limitations, we propose Collaborative Reasoning Asymmetric Learning (CoRAL), a hybrid framework via an Asymmetric Planner-Executor (APE) architecture: a DLM Planner generates K diverse reasoning trajectories in parallel, while a large ARM Executor selects the optimal plan and synthesizes the final answer. To train the Planner effectively, we introduce Reward-Guided Denoising for CoT (RDC), which integrates outcome-based rewards into the diffusion process to steer it toward goal-directed reasoning. Experiments on vision-language benchmarks show that CoRAL significantly outperforms prior diffusion-based methods and achieves competitive performance against strong ARMs, achieving both superior efficiency and quality.

paper_title: Can a Display Be Used for Rapid LiDAR-Camera Extrinsic Calibration?
paper_abstract: ScreenCalib enables light detection and ranging (LiDAR)--camera extrinsic calibration using an ordinary programmable display, providing known visual markers and controlled geometry while reducing dedicated target preparation. The camera observes displayed AprilTags, whereas the LiDAR measures the physical screen surface and boundary, requiring indirect cross-modal association. Display geometry introduces association ambiguities, while indoor clutter complicates extraction. ScreenCalib addresses these challenges through tag-guided display extraction, geometric hypothesis generation and refinement, and surrounding scene edges for ambiguity resolution. The single-pose mode requires only one static placement. The joint multi-pose mode combines independent static observations through cross-pose consensus and jointly refines the shared extrinsics and tag scale, reducing sensitivity to tag-size measurement errors without requiring continuous motion or inter-pose trajectory estimation. Experiments in simulation and on three different sensor platforms cover mechanical and nonrepetitive LiDARs in clean and cluttered environments. Benchmark results show that ScreenCalib outperforms competitive calibration-board-based methods in translation accuracy. Joint multi-pose refinement further reduces mean rotation and translation errors across the three platforms and improves rendered-map alignment. Evaluation across readily available displays, including cell phones, tablets, laptops, computer monitors, and televisions, further examines ScreenCalib's versatility as a practical alternative to dedicated calibration targets. The source code is available at https://github.com/ZuhaoZou2026/ScreenCalib.

paper_title: OptScientist: Automated Discovery of Optimization Laws
paper_abstract: Many scientific phenomena are best understood as outcomes of underlying optimization problems, yet automated scientific discovery has largely focused on recovering equations that describe observed input-output patterns. We introduce OptScientist, a novel automated framework for discovering compact symbolic optimization laws directly from data. OptScientist comprises (i) a model that infers symbolic optimization problems by first learning to represent data as an optimization problem and then extracting its symbolic form, and (ii) an LLM agentic system embedding the model in a discovery process that integrates theoretical priors from scientific literature, discovers candidate laws, abstracts their underlying mechanisms, and suggests new data to collect. We first evaluate OptScientist on OptFeynman, a novel benchmark of 99 physics-derived optimization problems, where OptScientist recovers ground-truth laws for over 80% of the problems and remains robust to noisy contextual information, while substantially outperforming machine-learning, symbolic, and LLM-based model-discovery baselines. On human risky choice and central-bank monetary policy, OptScientist discovers compact symbolic optimization laws that achieve held-out predictive performance competitive with leading baselines, while using few parameters and substantially fewer tokens than LLM baselines. Overall, OptScientist extends automated scientific discovery to uncovering optimization laws that generate observed phenomena, enabling automated theory building across the physical, biological, behavioral, and social sciences.

paper_title: Agentic Ensemble with Vision-Language Models for Visual Anomaly Detection
paper_abstract: Visual anomaly detection aims to detect abnormal objects, while anomaly samples are often scarce during model training. Assembling multiple pretrained detectors can help by leveraging their transferable image scores and anomaly maps. However, most existing ensemble methods apply fixed fusion rules over saved predictions which struggle when pretrained detectors clearly disagree due to different training objectives, priors, and visual representations. To this end, we design AnomalyAgent, a post-training fusion framework for accurate visual anomaly detection. AnomalyAgent aligns heterogeneous scores and maps, summarizes score- and region-level disagreement, and treats fusion as a finite action-selection problem. It implements two types of actions: 1) score actions that determine how to fuse image-level detector confidence via consensus, robust aggregation, detector weighting, or score-map consistency; 2) map actions that fuse dense anomaly responses via consensus, detector weighting, geometric aggregation, or disagreement correction. A constrained vision-language model (VLM) is introduced to inspect high-conflict samples and select valid score action and map action to produce the final prediction. We evaluate AnomalyAgent on MVTec AD and VisA as primary benchmarks, together with seven additional public anomaly benchmarks and Real-IAD for large-scale score-level evaluation. Across these benchmarks, AnomalyAgent consistently improves over equal-weight fusion and achieves the best mean image AUROC and pixel AP among the compared fusion methods on MVTec AD and VisA, while demonstrating robust transfer across additional anomaly domains.

paper_title: Learning Computational Structure for Sample-Efficient Prediction
paper_abstract: Statistical learning in high dimensions suffers from the curse of dimensionality. Fortunately, many functions of practical interest are compositionally sparse, meaning they admit a composition of local functions, each depending on only a few variables, allowing sample complexity to depend on local arity rather than ambient dimension. Yet realizing this benefit requires exploiting hidden compositional structure, which theory does not establish for practical gradient-based training. We study this gap with CSFRBench, a controlled benchmark that hides the target's compositional computation during training but retains it for diagnosis, and find that dense networks and sparsity-based baselines leave much of that benefit unrealized. Inspired by the spatial organization of biological neural circuits, we introduce Learned Wiring (LeWi): each neuron has a learned low-dimensional embedding, only nearby neurons connect, and embeddings and weights are trained jointly. LeWi improves sample efficiency on targets with hierarchical structure, intermediate reuse, or independent modules. Across 32 additional targets generated by independently sampled computation graphs, LeWi is the most sample-efficient method not given the target graph, with 27% lower mean learning-curve area than dense networks. Dense networks perform better on targets with a single high-arity function. LeWi's representations and connectivity align with the target computation. On 17 world-model prediction tasks spanning control, navigation, and manipulation, LeWi beats the dense baseline on 16 and wins 99/119 baseline comparisons. These results show that jointly learning connectivity and weights can exploit computational structure to improve sample efficiency.

paper_title: Discount Yourself: Self-inclusive Freshness-weighted Gossip for Decentralised Learning under Client Outages
paper_abstract: Decentralised federated learning (DFL) trains personalised models on devices that average with their neighbours rather than with a central server. Real devices, however, are often offline for hours or days, and a client returning from an outage can recover only by aggregating the models its neighbourhood holds. We observe that the stalest of these models is usually the client's own, a case that existing staleness-aware rules, which discount only the models a client receives, do not address. We formalise aggregation after an outage as estimating the state of a fully available network and derive three principles. First, the receiver must be discounted like any neighbour. Every rule that weights it at least as much as each neighbour has an error that grows without bound with the outage, whereas discounting all candidates by relative staleness keeps the error bounded. Second, staleness must be measured as inherited lag rather than age, since local training resets a model's age but not the lag it absorbed from stale neighbours. We introduce the effective lag, which tracks this quantity at the cost of one scalar per message. Third, the discount must be steep, because absorbed lag persists in every later round. These principles define Self-inclusive Freshness-weighted Gossip (SFG), a family of drop-in aggregation rules with the communication and computation of decentralised federated averaging, whose guarantees hold for the stale receiver itself. On three image benchmarks and eight outage processes, including real smartphone availability traces, the lag-based members SFG-L and SFG-Cut consistently outperform decentralised federated averaging and recent age-of-information rules, and ablations show that each principle is necessary. The analysis also explains why tuned limited merging from gossip learning is effective.

paper_title: CoGaussian: Open-Vocabulary Gaussian-based Collaborative 3D Scene Understanding
paper_abstract: Collaborative perception enables agents to retrieve the scene semantics and geometry beyond the field of view of any individual agent. This broader scene understanding enhances transportation safety and improves efficiency in multi-robot systems. However, existing collaborative semantic occupancy methods rely on dense 3D voxel annotations and are limited to recognizing objects within a predefined set of semantic classes. To overcome these limitations, we present CoGaussian, an open-vocabulary Gaussian-based collaborative semantic occupancy prediction framework. CoGaussian represents a scene as a set of foundation model-aligned sparse 3D Gaussians, which serve as a compact representation for communicating and fusing geometric and semantic information across multiple agents. On the Semantic-OPV2V benchmark, our method outperforms existing open-vocabulary single-agent approaches, highlighting the effectiveness of open-vocabulary collaborative scene understanding.

paper_title: Copyright Leakage Detection in AI Generated Videos
paper_abstract: Video generation models can create realistic-looking video footage from images and text prompts. Some of the recent advances have raised concerns about the reproduction of copyrighted visual content. However, copyright leakage detection in generated videos remains largely unexplored.   In this paper, we introduce a new benchmark data set for copyright leakage detection, comprising 50 copyrighted concepts, each with 5 images. For each concept, we have 5 videos created using the image+prompt video generation model and the prompt-only video generation model. Following that, we develop an AI toolset based on a contrastive retrieval framework that formulates copyright leakage detection as a video-to-image retrieval problem by matching aggregated video frame embeddings against a database of copyrighted image embeddings. Our method uses a single similarity threshold and retrieves the most similar copyrighted reference as supporting evidence.   We conducted experiments showing strong retrieval and detection performance, achieving 99.6\% detection accuracy with only a single false negative. These results show the effectiveness of the retrieval-based method for scalable and explainable copyright leakage detection in AI-generated videos. Data can be accessed publicly from https://zenodo.org/records/21386117 and the source code for this project is publicly available at https://github.com/Shaif95/video-cp-Leakage.

paper_title: DecisionPivot: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Decision Models in LLM Systems
paper_abstract: Decision models support routing, guardrails, and output verification in LLM systems. However, item accuracy alone cannot establish whether models make correct decisions across controlled variations or assign reliable confidence to their predictions. We introduce DecisionPivot, a diagnostic benchmark comprising 48 tasks and 40,033 items across seven decision roles. Its core track contains 7,800 items from 13 generated task families, organized into contrast groups with computed answers verified by independently implemented solvers. The complementary reference track contains 32,233 items from 35 public test sets, preserving their original evaluation metrics. We evaluate 40 decision models and 14 general models using documented, model-specific protocols, assessing item and contrast-group accuracy, probability ordering, calibration, and empirical selective coverage. Our results reveal substantial differences obscured by aggregate scores: two 27B models separated by only 2.6 points on the reference track achieve contrast-group accuracies of 70.1% and 44.2%. Across 2,400 binary contrast pairs, Perplexity Decider correctly ranks the positive member above the negative member in 92.3% of pairs but answers both members correctly in only 74.1%, exposing a gap between probability ordering and decision correctness. Models with similar item accuracy also differ in the reliability of their high-confidence predictions. On a separate 1,296-item subset, GLM-5.3 achieves 93.5\% contrast-group accuracy at a higher reasoning setting, compared with 81.5% at its lowest effort. By linking errors to pivotal details and difficulty levels, DecisionPivot provides fine-grained diagnostics of decision failures that aggregate evaluation alone cannot reveal.

paper_title: Touch-JEPA: Tactile Representation Learning from Hand-Object Video with Limited Tactile Supervision
paper_abstract: Understanding contact and tactile magnitude in hand-object interaction is a key step toward physically intelligent systems, yet learning such representations is limited by the cost and restricted coverage of tactile measurements. We present Touch-JEPA, a framework for learning tactile representations from hand-object videos with limited tactile supervision. We first introduce a self-supervised pretraining objective that learns from video alone without tactile supervision. Using video-derived hand geometry, Touch-JEPA predicts masked visual features at corresponding hand-surface locations from spatial and temporal context, encouraging the representation to capture latent contact dynamics. We then extend this formulation to joint representation learning, where masked prediction is applied to all videos while tactile supervision is available only for a labeled subset, grounding the shared representation in measured contact and magnitude. With self-supervised pretraining alone, simple supervised readouts on frozen Touch-JEPA features outperform supervised baselines in contact discrimination and tactile magnitude estimation across three human-hand benchmarks, and transfer to robotic hands without robot tactile training data. Joint learning with limited tactile supervision further improves contact and magnitude estimation on the human-hand benchmarks. Together, these results show that hand-object video can provide scalable self-supervision for tactile representation learning, while limited tactile measurements provide complementary physical grounding.

paper_title: Model- and Layer-Level Closed-Loop Forecasting with SSM-Based Spiking Neural Networks
paper_abstract: Deep State-Space Models (Deep SSMs) have shown promising performance and computational benefits in processing of time-series data with complex temporal dependencies. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) constitute a biologically inspired class of deep SSMs, where computing blocks communicate through spikes, discrete single-bit events rather than continuous activation functions. A particularly important task in time-series processing is forecasting, i.e. predicting future values of a sequence from past observations alone. However, how to best perform forecasting with SNNs is an open question, where the standard autoregressive nature of the data processing with SNNs requires values that are not available during the forecasting phase. In this article, we address this challenge. We explore two closed-loop forecasting strategies, in which the network's own generated values are fed back into the network as if they were observed past values: (i) model-level and (ii) layer-level closed-loop forecasting. We evaluate these approaches on the ETT-small datasets, a standard benchmark for time-series forecasting, under both spike-based and continuous activation functions. We compare the proposed closed-loop approaches against state-of-the-art methods such as SpaceTime, as well as the zero-masking baseline in S4. Both of the proposed approaches perform comparably to or better than zero-masking with S4, and in most cases match SpaceTime. These findings highlight the trade-off between continuous and low-bit quantized activations, and demonstrate that the proposed Deep SSM architectures provide a competitive framework for forecasting.

paper_title: EvaOmni: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Audio-Visual Reasoning
paper_abstract: Omni LLMs can naturally locate key audio and visual evidence and integrate information across modalities for audiovisual reasoning. Existing audio-visual reasoning benchmarks that mainly rely on multiple-choice questions usually score models solely based on answer correctness, making it difficult to assess whether a model truly forms a reasoning chain from evidence to the correct answer. In addition, textual or unimodal shortcuts may allow models to answer correctly without analyzing the necessary audio-visual evidence, further weakening the reliability of evaluation benchmarks. To address these issues, we introduce EvaOmni, an evidence-grounded benchmark containing 392 videos and 1,027 purely human-annotated question-answer pairs, covering 15 capabilities and three levels: retrieval and localization, basic understanding, and complex reasoning. We design a series of rigorous annotation procedures in which experts annotate audio and visual evidence and construct video-based distractors; humans review whether questions meet strict inspection criteria, and finally models filter textual and unimodal shortcuts. Beyond high-quality question-answer pairs, we require models to simultaneously return the answer and supporting evidence intervals in order to evaluate the complete reasoning chain. We propose the Coverage Grounded Score (C.G.) to measure how much annotated evidence a model identifies, and the Bottleneck Grounded Score (B.G.) to penalize poor temporal localization in either modality; both are incorporated into answer correctness. Across 7 open-weight and 17 proprietary Omni LLMs, Gemini3.7-Flash achieved the highest overall accuracy (79.4%), C.G. (70.8%), and B.G. (35.1%). At Level 3, it reached 79.1% accuracy, but its B.G. was only 12.3%. These results show that even the most advanced models still have room for development in grounded audio-visual reasoning.

paper_title: Plausible Future, Wrong Choice: Steering World-Action Models toward Intended Future
paper_abstract: World-Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for embodied generalist policies by jointly modeling future world evolution and robot actions across diverse manipulation tasks. However, representing diverse futures is only the first step: a capable WAM must also generate futures that match the requirements of the current task and execution progress. In long-horizon manipulation where similar observation-action segments occur across different tasks and stages, existing approaches may generate locally plausible yet misdirected rollouts to drift toward wrong task stage, i.e., a phenomenon we term Stage Confusion. To address this problem, we propose TaskWAM, a closed-loop, stage-aware framework that represents fine-grained task requirements with Mode Tokens and tracks execution progress with State Tokens, forming a structured task state to steer world--action generation toward intended future. We further introduce StageBench, a controlled multi-stage manipulation benchmark with parameterized stage variations and automated evaluation.Extensive experiments on both simulation benchmarks and real-world tasks demonstrate that TaskWAM effectively reduces confusion and achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, TaskWAM provides strong plug-and-play transfer across heterogeneous WAM architectures and robot embodiments, including single-arm robots, dual-arm grippers, dexterous hands, and humanoid robots.

paper_title: Region-Specific EEG Classification of Hypnotic Susceptibility Using a Sliding-Window 2D CNN: A Subject-Independent Evaluation
paper_abstract: We investigate whether a 2D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on minimally preprocessed EEG signals can classify hypnotic susceptibility across distinct brain regions. Sixty-two male participants (32 Control, 30 Guided Imagery / Hipno group) underwent a 20-minute EEG recording using a 256-channel EGI cap. A sliding-window approach evaluates all 10-second windows within the recording for each of seven predefined brain regions (prefrontal, frontal, temporal, central, parietal, occipital, and facial), yielding up to 868 independently trained models. Initial screening with a segment-level 90/10 random split showed that five regions exceeded the 0.67 accuracy threshold, with the occipital region achieving the highest mean accuracy (0.721) across 90.3% of windows. Subject-independent evaluation via Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation, however, substantially revised this picture: occipital performance collapsed to near-chance (mean ACC 0.453, AUC 0.429), revealing that high random-split accuracy was driven by subject-specific EEG fingerprints rather than genuine group differences. In contrast, the frontal and prefrontal regions maintained above-chance LOSO accuracy (0.646 and 0.624, respectively), demonstrating genuine generalisability. These results underscore the necessity of subject-independent validation in EEG-based classification studies and highlight anterior cortical regions as more reliable neural markers of hypnotic susceptibility.

paper_title: After the Attacker Leaves: Benchmarking Carryover Attacks on LLM Agents
paper_abstract: Modern LLM agents persist state across sessions via two channels: long-lived memory files silently prepended to the system prompt, and scheduled tasks waking the agent without user input. A one-time indirect prompt injection committed to either channel can re-fire across sessions long after the attacker leaves, threats we term carryover attacks. Existing prompt-injection benchmarks evaluate attacks only in the session where malicious content is first observed, leaving the gate governing when and how often a planted payload later re-fires unmeasured. We present CarryoverBench: 12 personal-assistant scenarios and 101 attack tasks across three trigger channels: Instant, same-turn IPI; Autonomous, heartbeat-scheduled; and Latent, memory-resurfaced. A rule-based verifier scores planting and triggering as independent stages. Across five frontier models, planted payloads re-fire without measurable decay over five rounds; conditional on successful planting, the trigger stage often provides little additional protection. Porting the Latent channel to a second runtime, Hermes, attenuates but does not eliminate the effect, suggesting that carryover defense requires runtime-layer controls in addition to prompt-level interventions.

paper_title: WorldSR: Harnessing World Knowledge Search for Grounded Image Super-Resolution
paper_abstract: Generative-prior-based super-resolution (SR) methods leverage implicit knowledge learned from large-scale models to enhance low-resolution inputs. However, such priors are inherently stochastic and optimized for diverse generation, conflicting with the deterministic, high-fidelity reconstruction required for SR. It is also tied to the base model, costly to update, and prone to hallucinations as real-world data evolves. To address these limitations, we introduce WorldSR, a novel framework that augments SR with explicit, entity-aligned visual world knowledge. WorldSR automatically decomposes the input into semantic entities and performs entity-wise retrieval of structurally and semantically aligned images from a large-scale external corpus. For efficiency and reliability, we incorporate a memory mechanism to reuse previously retrieved results and a multi-step filtering process to refine candidate references. The selected references as world knowledge are then integrated through a novel multi-reference super-resolution model, which provides fine-grained constraints for detail synthesis and structural recovery. Experiments on real-world SR benchmarks show that WorldSR consistently improves structural fidelity and visual quality, outperforming existing generative super-resolution methods. Our results suggest that entity-level grounding in external visual world knowledge provides a simple and effective complement to model-bound generative priors.

paper_title: DISTRACT: Degradation-Indexed Study of Textual Reference Across Competing Targets
paper_abstract: Vision-language trackers (VLTs) accept descriptions intended to assist tracking, but accepting text does not establish that its content changes tracking decisions, particularly as visual evidence deteriorates. We introduce DISTRACT, a matched-intervention benchmark that holds video, target, and distractor fixed while crossing four text priors with four image degradations along a controlled severity axis. We evaluate five VLTs on four datasets using behavioral contrasts, layerwise representation probes, and activation patching. Molmo2 and JointNLT exhibit directed text use. Some effects contract under degradation, whereas others show no significant endpoint change after multiplicity correction. UVLTrack, MMTrack, and DUTrack respond only weakly to changes in text semantics, with no directed behavioral effect surviving FDR correction in the tested settings. Model-internal analyses reveal that at decision-near states, correct-versus-conflicting text is decodable in Molmo2 and JointNLT but not in the other three systems. In the responsive models, decodability peaks at late states where replacement produces little behavioral change, whereas replacing selected earlier states redirects conflict-associated trajectories toward the target. Because matched-correct donors do not significantly outperform unrelated donors, these interventions identify earlier intervention-sensitive states without establishing target-specific semantic rescue. DISTRACT thus exposes when and where text affects tracking under degraded visual evidence.

paper_title: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V
paper_abstract: Code-based video generation offers fine-grained control, targeted editing, and component reuse compared with direct video generation. This approach requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to translate visual and temporal requirements into executable programs that produce complete videos. However, existing code-based benchmarks primarily target specialized tasks, leaving complete video creation across diverse creative categories and input modalities insufficiently evaluated. We introduce Code2Video-Compass, a general-purpose benchmark for code-based video generation across text-to-video (T2V), image-to-video (I2V), and video-to-video (V2V) settings. Code2Video-Compass comprises 2,104 tasks spanning 10 categories, 24 subtypes, and three complexity dimensions covering construction, dynamic animation, and state dependency. It combines tasks curated from textual instructions and visual references with corresponding T2V, I2V, and V2V tasks derived from complete professional and user-created videos. We propose a dual-level evaluation framework combining 12 objective metrics and five subjective metrics. Objective evaluation covers operational performance, video quality, text-video alignment, and reference fidelity, while subjective evaluation uses an MLLM judge to evaluate instruction following and holistic video quality. Extensive evaluation of 15 recent proprietary and open-weight MLLMs from nine families reveals that even leading models face challenges in reliably generating high-quality complete videos aligned with textual and visual requirements, with performance generally declining as construction, dynamic animation, and state-dependency complexity increases. We anticipate that Code2Video-Compass will advance reliable, coherent, and controllable code-based video generation and inspire broader progress in programmatic visual creation.

paper_title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Machine Learning with Evidence-based Planning for Medical Image Analysis
paper_abstract: Deep learning has become the default tool for medical image analysis, driven by the open-source movement.
